chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Asad ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Hamza who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman — what she can own from her relatives. He said: Everyone, except five: her father, her mother, her son, her daughter, and her husband.

key_terms.تملك: To own/possess (in the legal sense of ownership over a person)
key_terms.خمسة: Five — referring to the five specific categories of relatives exempt from ownership

ai.seo_question: Can a woman own her relatives as slaves in Islamic law? Who are the five relatives exempt from ownership?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on the question of whom a woman may own as a slave from among her own relatives, stating that she may own anyone except five specific categories of mahram relatives: her father, mother, son, daughter, and husband. This ruling reflects the Islamic legal principle that ownership of certain close relatives is automatically nullified — a slave becomes free upon entering such a close familial relationship with the owner. The question arose in the context of Shia jurisprudence on slavery and familial bonds.
